dlc.s01.title: The Search
dlc.s01.summary: May 7, 2024. Gotō tweets: I really have lost it. Ayaka died the day before yesterday, yesterday I went offline to look for Spr's whereabouts, today I get up and — Schedule II!
beats: May 7, 2024, Gotō tweets: I really have lost it. Ayaka died the day before yesterday, yesterday I went offline to look for Spr's whereabouts, today I get up and — Schedule II!
I'm going to start looking for Jing.
He went looking for traces of Spring. Someone later identified it: those were the traces of following the spring wind "turning into wind" at a certain university.
Spring had been dead for over a year, but Gotō was still looking for him. The DLC is framed by this search: a living person looking back at a dead guide.

dlc.s02.title: Scratch Paper
dlc.s02.summary: June 4, 2022, 18:17. Spring sends his first tweet: no self-introduction — think of me however you like.
beats: June 4, 2022, 18:17. Spring sent his first tweet: no self-introduction. Think of me however you like.
It depends on you, not on me.
The next day, on scratch paper. He writes four methods for making methamphetamine from ephedrine;
compares the chemical structures of tryptamines and amphetamines — serotonin, DMT, meth, cathinone — and from that infers a few designer drugs;
explains the nature of MAOIs, and describes caffeine's psychoactive action.
He writes: because of the "phat" effect, monoamines hit a ceiling at a certain point... attach a methyl group, make it amphetamine, and route around oxidation.
He writes: stimulant plus hallucinogen is roughly MDMA.
A high-schooler, working pharmacology out into his own universe on scratch paper. Intellect was his pride — and the door through which the thing that later killed him came in.

dlc.s03.title: The Guide
dlc.s03.summary: With his chemistry and pharmacology he became the first generation of od guides.
beats: With his chemistry and pharmacology he became the first generation of od guides.
He wrote up the general experience and side effects for people who wanted to try dextromethorphan: six tablets, vision sharper, hearing sharper, attention focused;
twelve tablets, a floating feeling, dizziness, anxiety, irritability; twenty-four tablets, nausea, a dry mouth, a bitter mouth.

He wrote about his own experience: the last time he took a box with no effect, took another box, and then some time later slid into the od feeling out of nowhere — floating, unsteady walking, pupils dilated,
gone in about ten minutes — I think it's called a flashback?
Then he tries to talk people out of it. Important thing, say it three times: don't od dextromethorphan regularly, don't od dextromethorphan regularly, don't od dextromethorphan regularly.
If you think I'm being childish, just block me. But personally I think this does some good for people who abuse drugs.
And then: I will never od dextromethorphan again even if you kill me. My whole self feels like it's been rendered an idiot.
I also advise anyone who is or wants to od dextromethorphan: take too much and you really do become an idiot. Even if you od caffeine or psychiatric meds, don't od this.
But on June 14 he writes again: should I spend my saved pocket money on some caffeine lozenges to play with? Overdose, yay. Before I finish writing — mm, I'm going to eat first.
The tear between knowing and doing. He talks others out of it while exploring the drugs himself. This isn't hypocrisy; it's a clever person who hasn't yet learned to be afraid.

dlc.s04.title: Knowing and Not Knowing
dlc.s04.summary: He has intellectual honesty. At first I said: everyone addicted to meth is an idiot. Now I find I was wrong.
beats: He has intellectual honesty. At first I said, people addicted to meth are idiots. Now I find I was wrong.
Back then I looked down on meth users, thought what's the point of meth, hallucinogens are better. After digging deeper I started fantasising about what the pleasure of "skiing" would be like.
Now I find I'm the clown.
He had awe for opioids: if I touched opioids I'd either be remaking myself this life or in rehab; opioid withdrawal means methadone for life,
and after that, once I'm in withdrawal, I'm afraid my whole body will feel like ants crawling.
But he had no awe for the combination of hallucinogens and stimulants.

That line was drawn in the wrong place: he feared opioid withdrawal, but not the blood pressure and chaos of MAOI plus ephedrine plus ayahuasca. The foreshadowing of his cause of death is buried here.
He also lost control. When mania hit, he couldn't help wanting to curse people, to vent, to destroy something, to smash things; he couldn't stay quiet.
And right when the mania hit, it also occurred to him — why not just remake — although I really don't like hearing myself say the word remake,
because I once told myself a bad life beats a good death.
That time I drove to the riverside ready to remake, and then the mood just went down like a rollercoaster for no reason, and it felt like nothing had happened,
and I felt blank too, and then I drove back, lol. Thinking about it now I still find it lol.
The survival instinct and the loss of control in one body. That time at the river he was blank himself: why didn't I jump? He doesn't know. The reader doesn't either.
That "don't know" is the exact reverse of that night later — that night he "knew" too much, and was too sure of what he knew.

dlc.s05.title: Gentleness
dlc.s05.summary: The side that got overlooked. I'm so sorry to my friend — I made him a promise and didn't keep it. I made him angry, and I feel like saying ten thousand sorries.
beats: The side that got overlooked. I'm so sorry to my friend — I made him a promise and didn't keep it. I even made him angry. I feel like saying ten thousand sorries.
He wasted his time writing me a note about my personality problem, and in the end I couldn't even keep his promise.
I apologised and he wasn't angry; he just felt sad. It hurt so much. I wanted to smash my head into a wall and pass out. He did so much for me and I couldn't even keep a promise.
He wants to be alone. I really wish I could be alone. If you asked me when I'm happiest at home, I'd say without hesitation: when I'm home alone.
If I'm playing games and get heard, I get sent off to do all sorts of things, and if I don't want to, I get scolded for playing games all day.
I'll probably forget about it in a bit. I really am an idiot who can't control his emotions.
Good thing I can't remember things. If I could remember, I'd probably blow up one day and just remake, haha.
And the high school entrance exam.
A friend remembers: at the 2022 entrance exam, Spring came over to say hi with a dextromethorphan box balanced on his head, and went into the exam on caffeine lozenges and dextro.
To this day we still don't know what Spring heard in the English listening test.
The gentle hello and the reckless dosing in the same frame. This is a boy who'd say ten thousand sorries to a friend, and who'd walk into the exam hall with a pill box balanced on his head.
He isn't a symbol. He's a person.

dlc.s06.title: The Ayahuasca Night
dlc.s06.summary: January 8, 2023. Reckless link by link, every link avoidable:
beats: January 8, 2023. Reckless link by link, every one of them avoidable:
18:15, he boiled harmala. At noon he'd got the acacia bark he bought on Xianyu. 14:33, he swallowed an asthma tablet (ephedrine).
17:26, he accidentally wet the bark, took out another portion and broke it up bare-handed, exhausted, hands bleeding from the work.
19:47, he drank down the ayahuasca that had been simmering in the pot for over an hour and a half. 20:11, violent distortion.
Compounding factors: the acacia bark was also rich in the chaotic 5-MeO-DMT "toad toxin", and the ayahuasca had been boiled too long, which put him in confusion;
the ephedrine's high blood pressure combined with harmala, bursting blood vessels, cerebral haemorrhage, organ rupture, heart failure;
the bark had probably been sprayed with all kinds of pesticide by a plant-protection worker, poisoning him and speeding up death;
he didn't put the knives away — in the hallucination of fear and pain at the end, what sprayed across the wall was his own blood from self-harm.

Spring's father sensed something wrong and rushed into the room. They tried to revive him for a long time; there was no bringing him back. The final cause of death was total organ failure from poisoning.
It wasn't dying for an ideal. It's a clever person stacking too many avoidable links together, and every one of them landing.

dlc.s07.title: Spring's Father
dlc.s07.summary: A broken father, having lost his beloved son, concludes that Spring killed himself, and questions Spring's classmates: was he bullied at school? Why did he kill himself?
beats: A broken father, having lost his beloved son, concluded that Spring had killed himself, and questioned Spring's classmates: was he bullied at school? Why did he kill himself?
He got nothing.
Spring's funeral was held in February 2023.
The father's unanswerable question sits next to the record's clear cause of death: he wants to know "why", and the record can only answer "how".
Why would a boy who'd say ten thousand sorries to a friend boil himself to death? The record doesn't answer why. It only leaves how — and that why that can never be asked.

dlc.s08.title: A Brief Spring Breeze
dlc.s08.summary: A brief spring breeze. The spring wind blew itself out.
beats: A brief spring breeze. The spring wind blew itself out.
But the guide left behind the three-times-repeated warning, the derivations on scratch paper, the ten thousand sorries to a friend, the pill box balanced on his head in the exam hall.
These aren't evidence of martyrdom. They're evidence of a person who lived.
